s: Install Library first, then follow the first steps in Install.

Bookmarks, apps, folders, and terminal commands open from the menu bar, a keyboard shortcut, or Spotlight. To open an item the other way, hold Option while you click it. Bookmarks open in a new tab or a new window. Apps come to the front. To start a new copy, add a launch argument, such as --profile work. Terminal commands run in a login shell in a new Terminal window. Add only commands you trust.
Quick Open is a search box that floats over your screen. It searches your library, your clipboard history, and your snippets, and it runs the result you choose.

Press ⌃Space. This is the default shortcut. Type to search. The search field has the keyboard as soon as Quick Open opens. Press Return, or click a row, to run it. Quick Open closes. Press the same shortcut again to close Quick Open without choosing anything. Quick Open also opens with the library://search address. Quick Open appears centered on the screen under the pointer. It stays in place whil

Quick Open splits your text into words. Each word must match something about the item, and every word must match for the item to appear. Library items and snippets are scored for each word: Match Score The start of the name, or the start of a keyword 4 Anywhere inside the name 3 Target, folder, or keywords (including the color) 2 The letters in order inside the name, with others between them 1 An

t: What appears with an empty search
s: What appears with an empty search With the search field empty, Quick Open shows, in order: Suggested: the link or app on the clipboard, or a link selected in the app in front, when it is not in your library yet. See Add a suggested link or app. Frequently Used: up to five items you have opened at least twice. The whole library, in the same order as the Library menu. Clipboard: the five first clipb

What appears with a search With text in the search field, results appear in these groups, each with its own heading: Top Hit: the first result. Return runs it. Library: matching items. Clipboard: up to eight matching clipboard items, pinned items first, then newest first. Snippets: matching snippets. Suggestions: a web address you typed, or a suggested link or app. Clipboard matches must contain e

Web addresses If the search text is a web address, Quick Open adds two rows: Open followed by the host, for example Open example.com. Add "example.com" to Library. A web address has no spaces. It is either a full address with://, or a host name with a dot and a top-level domain of at least two letters, such as example.com/path. localhost is not treated as a web address.

t: Add a suggested link or app
s: Add a suggested link or app When the clipboard holds a web link or an application that is not in your library, Quick Open offers to add it. It is listed under Suggested with an empty search. It is also listed when the search is at least two characters long and is part of the words "add to library", such as ad or to li. A link selected in the app in front is used first, if Quick Open can read it. C

Search only one app's copies Type from and the name of an app to see only the clipboard items you copied while that app was in front. For example, from Safari shows Safari copies. Add words after the app name to search those copies, such as from Safari invoice. The name must match an app that appears in your clipboard history, ignoring case. When two apps match, the longer name wins. When the sear

Key What it does Up or Down arrow Moves the selection. It stops at the first and last row. Return or Enter Runs the selected row. Quick Open closes, except when the row opens a submenu. ⌥Return Opens a library item the other way. See the note below. ⌘1 to ⌘9 Runs the first to ninth row. The number shows at the right of each row. Tab Shows the actions for the selected row. Tab again returns to the

⌥Return For a library item that can open two ways, ⌥Return does the opposite of the item's usual setting: A web bookmark opens in a new tab, or in a new window. An app is brought forward, or a new instance is started. The labels in the actions list name the two ways. For clipboard items and snippets, ⌥Return does the same as Return. Option-click does not change how a row opens in Quick Open. Use ⌥

Space Space previews the selected clipboard item in Quick Look, when the search field is empty. Press Space again, or Escape, to close the preview. With text in the search field, Space always types a space. With an empty search, Space types a space when the selected row is not a clipboard item, or when the clipboard item has nothing to preview.

Press Tab, or right-click a row, to see its actions. The actions depend on the row. Library item (a bookmark, app, command, or folder item): Open, and the other way to open the item, where it applies. Copy Link, for a bookmark. Copy Clean Link, for a bookmark. It removes tracking parameters such as utm_source, fbclid, and gclid. The saved link is not changed. Copy as Markdown Link, for a bookmark.

The right side of Quick Open shows the selected row in full. It is 280 points wide. Clipboard text: the first 4,000 characters, selectable, with the source app, time, and size. Picture: the picture. A GIF plays. Files: each file's name and icon. Other copies: the number of formats. Library item: its name, icon, and link, command, or path. Its folder appears under it. Snippet: its name and the firs

Setting Where Default Effect Show Quick Open Settings > Shortcuts ⌃Space The key that opens Quick Open. Paste into text fields Settings > Clipboard On Clipboard items paste, not just copy, when a text field has the keyboard as Quick Open opens. Needs Accessibility access. Require Touch ID or password to show pinned items Settings > Clipboard Off Locked pinned items show only as Pinned Item, and se

Clipboard matches in a search: eight. Clipboard items with an empty search: five. Frequently Used: five items, each opened at least twice. Text in a clipboard item is searched up to its first 100,000 characters. The preview shows the first 4,000 characters of text. Each row is 42 points tall. The list shows about seven or eight rows at once and scrolls for the rest.

t: What it stores and whether it syncs
s: Quick Open stores nothing of its own. It reads the library, clipboard history, snippets, and open counts. Where each one is kept, and whether it syncs, is in Storage and sync.

Quick Open closes when another app comes to the front, when the Spotlight search opens, or when you click elsewhere. It stays open while the Quick Look preview has the keyboard, and while the Touch ID or password prompt is up. A row can be dragged into another app. A clipboard image, file, link, or text is dropped as that type, and Quick Open closes after the drop.

Click the Library icon in the menu bar to open the menu. To open it at the pointer, press the Show Library Menu shortcut. Settings > Shortcuts > Library menu opens decides where it appears. Update Available. Appears at the top when a newer version exists. Choose it to see the update options. See Stay up to date. Your items. Bookmarks, apps, terminal commands, folders, and dividers, in the order yo

Library has two kinds of shortcut: Global shortcuts work in every app. They open the Library menu, Quick Open, the clipboard menu, and the link you copied last. Item shortcuts open one bookmark, application, or terminal command from anywhere. You set them in Get Info. Both kinds can be a key combination, a modified click, a scroll, a pinch, a swipe, or a hot corner.

Shortcut Default Set in Show Library Menu Control and right-click Settings > Shortcuts Show Quick Open ⌃Space Settings > Shortcuts Show Clipboard Menu ⌃⌘V Settings > Shortcuts Open Copied Link none Settings > Shortcuts Item shortcuts have no defaults. Each item starts with none. The Settings page lists the four global shortcuts under those names. Open Copied Link opens the web link you copied last

Defaults on first launch The first time a version with these defaults runs, the Library menu and Quick Open get their defaults if they have none, and the clipboard menu gets ⌃⌘V. After that first run, clearing a shortcut sticks.

t: Change or clear a global shortcut
s: Open Settings > Shortcuts. Click the shortcut field. It reads Record Shortcut and then Press a shortcut…, with an outline around it. Press the keys you want. The shortcut is saved as soon as you press it. To cancel without changing anything, press Escape or click anywhere else. To clear a shortcut, click the … button next to the field and choose Clear. The … menu also sets a hot corner. Clear is a

Kind How you record it Rule Key combination Press the keys Hold Control, Option, or Command. Shift alone does not count. Modified click Hold a modifier and click a button other than the left button At least one modifier. Right click and middle click have names. Other buttons show as "Button" and their number. Scroll Hold a modifier and scroll At least one modifier. Scroll Up, Down, Left, or Right.

Set item shortcuts in Get Info, in the Shortcuts section. The section appears for bookmarks, applications, and terminal commands. It does not appear for folders or dividers. Select the item and press ⌘I. Choose Add Shortcut. A new row starts recording. Press the keys, click with a modifier, scroll, pinch, swipe, or choose a hot corner from the … menu. Repeat to add more shortcuts. An item can have

A shortcut can be in use by macOS or by another app. Library cannot always tell. Key combinations: if the system refuses a key combination, Library shows an orange warning triangle with the tooltip In use by another app. You see it next to the global shortcut in Settings > Shortcuts, and in the Shortcut column in Edit Library next to the item. ⌃Space can conflict with the macOS input source shortc

A hot corner runs a shortcut when the pointer reaches a corner of a screen. In a shortcut field, open the … menu. Choose Hot Corner, then one of Top Left Corner, Top Right Corner, Bottom Left Corner, or Bottom Right Corner. A hot corner fires when the pointer reaches a spot within about two points of the corner, and only when no modifier key is held. It fires again only after the pointer has moved

Click, scroll, pinch, and swipe shortcuts need Accessibility access. Key combinations and hot corners do not. To turn it on, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility and allow Library. Library also shows a Grant Access… button in Get Info and an Allow… button in Settings when access is missing. Until access is granted, those shortcuts do nothing. Library checks again every few sec

t: Terminal commands run without a confirmation
s: By default, a terminal command runs in a new Terminal window as soon as its shortcut is pressed, when it is opened from Spotlight, or when it opens at login. Library does not ask first. To ask first, turn on Confirm Terminal Commands in Settings > General. Library then shows the command and waits. Cancel is the default button, so pressing Return cancels. The URL scheme never runs a command. The Sh
Global shortcuts stay on this Mac. Item shortcuts are saved with the item. Where each kind of data is kept is in Storage and sync.
Four hot corners, each set from the … menu. Restore Defaults does not change item shortcuts or Open Copied Link. Escape cancels a recording only when no modifier key is held.

Library keeps a history of what you copy. You can copy an item back, paste it into a text field, pin the items you keep, and queue several items to paste in order. The history is reached from the clipboard menu, from the Clipboard submenu in the Library menu, and from Quick Open.

Library records each copy with every format it was copied in, so copying an item back loses nothing. It records: Text, and links. A link is text that is a web address. Images. A copied image is kept in one format, PNG when there is one. Files, by name and icon. Screenshots and screen recordings, when Add screenshots and recordings is on. See Screenshots and recordings. Any other copy, which shows

When Add screenshots and recordings is on, Library adds each new screenshot and screen recording to the clipboard history as soon as macOS saves it. Take five screenshots, and all five are in the history, ready to paste. Screenshots are added as images, in the same way as a copied image. Recordings are added as a link to the file. Library does not copy the recording, because recordings are large.

Pinned items stay in the history after you quit, and they are never removed by the limits below. In Quick Open, find the item, and press Tab. Choose Pin. To remove the pin, press Tab on the item again and choose Unpin. Pins are set in Quick Open only. Pinned items show first in the clipboard menu, under Pinned, and first in Quick Open.

Press ⌃⌘V. The menu opens at the pointer. Choose an item to copy it back, or press a number key from 1 to 9 to choose one of the first nine items. Hold Option over a rich-text item. Its entry changes to Copy as Plain Text, and choosing it copies the text without formatting. The menu lists pinned items under Pinned and the 20 most recent other items under Recent. It has Clear History at the bottom.

t: The Clipboard submenu in the Library menu
s: The Clipboard submenu in the Library menu The Clipboard submenu in the Library menu lists the ten first items, pinned items first. Choosing one copies it. It never pastes. It has Clear History, and the paste queue when the queue has items.

When Paste into text fields is on, choosing an item from Quick Open or the clipboard menu pastes it, if a text field had the keyboard when the menu or Quick Open opened. Otherwise it copies the item. Library checks for a text field as the menu or Quick Open opens. When you then choose an item, Library presses ⌘V in the app in front, a moment later. This needs Accessibility access. Without it, choo

Use the paste queue to paste several items in order. In Quick Open, find an item, press Tab, and choose Add to Paste Queue. Repeat for each item. The queue lists them in order in the clipboard menu. Choose Paste Next in the clipboard menu. Library copies the first item and removes it from the queue. Press ⌘V in the app you are working in. Repeat from step 3 for the next item. Clear Queue removes e

Copy as turns a text item into a new clipboard entry. The original stays in the history as it was. In Quick Open, find a text item, press Tab, and choose Copy as…. Choose one of the options: Plain Text copies the text without formatting. Trimmed Whitespace removes spaces and line breaks at both ends. Lowercase and Uppercase change the case. Joined Lines turns each line break into a space. Smart Pu

Use Markdown links to paste a title and its address in a document. In Quick Open, find a bookmark, or a copied link, press Tab, and choose Copy as Markdown Link. Paste into a Markdown document. The result is [Title](address). The title is the bookmark's name, or the copied link's host. Characters that have a meaning in Markdown are escaped. Spaces and parentheses in the address are percent-encoded

t: Filter by the app you copied from
s: Each copy records the app that was in front when you copied it. You can list only the copies made in one app. Open Quick Open. Type from and the app's name, such as from Safari. Add words after the name to search those copies, such as from Safari invoice. The name matches an app in your history, ignoring case. Copies made while Library itself was in front have no app name, so they do not appear in

t: Quick Look and the Space key
s: Quick Look shows a clipboard item in the system preview panel. In Quick Open, select a clipboard item, with the search field empty, and press Space. Keys for closing it are in Keyboard. In Quick Open, press Tab, and choose Quick Look. Text and pictures are shown from a temporary copy. Files are shown where they are. Items with nothing to show, such as a format Library does not display, cannot be p

For a text item, Quick Open's Tab actions also include three actions that work on the text. Each appears only when the text has the matching thing in it: Open in Maps opens an address in Apple Maps. Copy Phone Number copies the number with its digits and plus sign only. Add to Calendar opens Calendar's add-event sheet for a date or time. The event's title is the first line of the text. An event wi

Browsers copy a still picture when you copy an animated GIF. With Play copied GIFs on, Library downloads the original GIF from the page, so it plays in the list and the preview. The setting is off by default. It applies to copies made while it is on. It does not download GIFs for copies you made earlier. Library asks the page's server for the GIF file only. It sends no cookies, and it stops after

The lock asks for Touch ID or your Mac password before pinned items are shown or copied. Open Settings > Clipboard. Turn on Require Touch ID or password to show pinned items. Library will not turn the lock on when your Mac has neither Touch ID nor a password. Add a password in System Settings, then turn it on again. With the lock on: A locked pinned item shows a lock icon and the words Pinned Item

By default, unpinned history is kept in memory and is gone when Library quits. Pinned items are always kept. To keep unpinned history: Open Settings > Clipboard. Turn on Keep clipboard history across restarts. With this on: The unpinned history is saved to a file when a copy is made, about a second after it. Copies from password managers and copies marked private are never saved. Images over 5 MB

Setting Where Default Effect Keep clipboard history Settings > Clipboard On Records copies. Turning it off stops recording. Items already in the history stay until you quit or clear them. Paste into text fields Settings > Clipboard On Choosing an item pastes it when a text field has the keyboard. Needs Accessibility access. Play copied GIFs Settings > Clipboard Off Downloads the GIF behind a copie

Unpinned items: the 50 most recent. Pinned items are not counted. Memory: the history holds up to 200 MB in total, including pinned items. When the total is over, the oldest unpinned items are removed first. Each copy: up to 25 MB. A larger copy is not recorded. Search: the first 100,000 characters of each text item are searched. Saved images: 5 MB each, when history is kept across restarts. Clipb

t: What it stores and whether it syncs
s: Clipboard history stays on this Mac and does not sync, even with Keep Library in iCloud Drive on. Where each part is kept is in Storage and sync.

Turning off Keep clipboard history stops recording. It does not clear what is already in the history. A copy is recorded about half a second after you make it. Hold Option for Copy as Plain Text only works on rich-text items in the clipboard menu. Other items do not offer that choice. The paste queue is cleared when Library quits. Quick Look temporary copies are removed when Library starts, so a p

Edit Library is the window where you manage everything in your library: add, move, sort, search, edit, delete, merge, import, and back up. Open it from the Library menu with Edit Library…. The window itself is titled "Library."
Click the Library icon in the menu bar. Choose Edit Library…. The window opens at the size and position you last left it. It cannot be smaller than 680 by 320 points.

Toolbar: Edit… (⌘I), Add (the + menu), Snippets, Get Info, Share, and Delete. Edit, Get Info, and Delete need a selection. Share works for one selected item that has a link or an application. It is off for templates and terminal commands. Columns: Name, Shortcut, and Path. Path shows the address, the command, or the application path, with its arguments. Sort menu (the arrows at the right of the he

Choose + in the toolbar, or use File > New: Item Shortcut What you enter Bookmark ⌘N Name and URL (both required) Application none Pick from the installed applications, with optional arguments Terminal Command none Name and command (both required) Folder ⇧⌘N Name Divider none Name Every sheet has a Folder menu. Choose Top level or an existing folder. You can also drag items into the window: Drag a

Click a row to select it. Shift-click and Command-click select several rows, as in other Mac lists. Double-click a single row to open it. Press Return to rename the selected row. Press Escape or Return to finish. Press ⌘I, or choose Edit… from the toolbar or the right-click menu, to open Get Info. With several rows selected, Get Info opens the bulk edit sheet.

Click a column heading to sort by it. The first click sorts ascending, the second descending, and the third returns to Your Order. An arrow shows the column in use. Choose the sort menu, then Your Order, Name, Path, Most Used, or Recently Opened. Name and Path start ascending. Shortcut sorts by the first shortcut of each item. Items with no shortcut sort last. Path sorts by the address, or the com

Type in the search field at the top right of the window. The prompt reads "Name, URL, command, or keyword." Each word you type must match. For example, jira ops finds an item only if both words appear in its name, URL, command, or keywords. A folder whose name matches shows all of its contents. Any other folder shows only the items inside it that match. Dividers never match. Recently Deleted is fi

Drag onto a folder to move the selected rows into it. Drag onto a row that is not a folder to place the dragged rows directly before it. This works only in Your Order. While a column or the sort menu sorts the list, a drop before a row does nothing. Drag onto empty space to move the rows to the top level. Move to in the right-click menu lists Top level and every folder. Items that would end up ins

The menu groups its commands as follows: Open, Open All (folders only), Show in Finder (applications only). Edit…, Rename. Add to Reading List, Mark as Read, Mark as Unread, Remove from Reading List, as they apply. Move to, Share…. Delete, alone at the bottom. In Recently Deleted, the menu offers only Restore and Delete Immediately. Open All opens each bookmark and application in a folder, one aft

Select one item and press ⌘I, or choose Edit…. Get Info has one section for each kind of item. Only the fields that apply to the item are shown. All items Name (required). Icon: choose Choose… to pick an SF Symbol or an emoji. The popover has Symbols and Emoji tabs, a search field, recent choices, and Use Default. The default is the site's icon for a bookmark, the application's icon for an applica

Templates A template is a bookmark whose address has a value that you type each time you open it. A named field is plain text unless you declare it. {project} and {id:Issue number} become fields only when their names are listed in Fields, such as project, id:Issue number. Without that, Library shows the text exactly as typed. In Get Info for a bookmark, turn on Ask for a value when opening. The ad

Bulk edit Select several rows and choose Edit… (or ⌘I). Bulk edit changes only Icon, Color, and Opens In. The bulk sheet changes only the fields you set. Each field starts at Don't Change. Icon: Don't Change, Default, or Custom, then Choose… for a symbol or emoji. Color: Don't Change, None, or a color. Shown only when at least one selected item can have a color. Dividers are skipped. Opens In: sho

Use the Reading List to save bookmarks to read later. Right-click one or more bookmarks. Choose Add to Reading List. Items in the list appear in a Reading List section at the top, unread first, then read. Each one also stays in its folder in the library. Use the right-click menu to Mark as Read, Mark as Unread, or Remove from Reading List. Removing an item from the Reading List leaves it in your l

Deleting moves items to Recently Deleted, so you can get them back. To delete, use the Delete key, ⌘Delete, the toolbar's Delete button, or Delete in the right-click menu. Folders go with their contents. Undo is one step named Delete. Restore puts an item back in its folder. If that folder no longer exists, the item goes to the top level. Undo is one step named Restore. Delete Immediately removes

Choose File > Find Duplicates… to find bookmarks and applications that open the same thing. Two bookmarks are duplicates when they have the same address and the same browser. The comparison ignores differences in the case of the scheme and host and a trailing slash, and it treats a missing https:// as https://. The path and query keep their case. Two applications are duplicates when they are the s

Choose File > Import Bookmarks… to bring in bookmarks from Safari or Chrome. Choose the bookmarks file in the open panel: Safari: Bookmarks.plist in ~/Library/Safari. Chrome: the Bookmarks file in ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default. Press ⇧⌘G in the panel to type a path. Library adds the bookmarks in one folder, named Imported from Safari or Imported from Chrome. Folders keep thei

Choose File > Check Links to check every bookmark now. Each address is checked at most once a day. An address that was checked in the last 24 hours is skipped. Up to four addresses are checked at a time. Library first sends a HEAD request, which asks only for the headers. If the server refuses it, Library sends a GET request and reads up to 64 KB of the page to decide. A bookmark whose page return

Export and restore are in two places. Export File > Export Library… or Settings > General > Backup > Export…. The file is named Library Backup followed by the date, in JSON. The backup has your bookmarks, folders, shortcuts, icons, keywords, colors, templates, and Open at Login settings. Items in Recently Deleted are not exported. Clipboard items are not exported. Pinned clipboard items are encryp

Action Key New Bookmark ⌘N New Folder ⇧⌘N Edit… (Get Info) ⌘I Delete (to Recently Deleted) Delete, or ⌘Delete Rename Return, with one row selected Undo ⌘Z Redo ⇧⌘Z These keys work while the Library window is in front. Apart from ⌘N, ⇧⌘N, and ⌘I, the File menu items have no key.

t: Where your data is stored and whether it syncs
s: The library is kept in bookmarks.json, and it syncs when Keep Library in iCloud Drive is on. Where each kind of data is kept is in Storage and sync.

Undo uses the Library window's undo history. Edits made before the window has been opened in this session are not undoable. Changes that come from another Mac or from iCloud clear the undo history. Recently Deleted keeps items for 30 days. Open All asks before opening more than five items. This threshold is fixed at five. There is no setting for it. Open All skips terminal commands, templates, div

Settings > General > Name new bookmarks from their pages: off by default. When it is on, a new bookmark takes its page's title. Settings > General > Check links periodically: off by default. Settings > General > Keep Library in iCloud Drive: off by default. Settings > General > Backup: Export and Restore. Settings > General > Open at login must be on for Open When You Log In on an item to do anyth

Terminal commands marked Open When You Log In run in Terminal when Library opens at login. They run without a confirmation unless Confirm Terminal Commands is on. See Keyboard shortcuts for the other places a command runs. Bulk edit does not change names, addresses, keywords, notes, or shortcuts. Sorting is not saved between launches. The Library menu item is Edit Library…, and the window is title

A color is a dot that helps you sort items at a glance. Use colors to organize your library, not to show status. Library has seven colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, and gray. Set a color. Select an item, press ⌘I to open Get Info, and choose a dot under Color. Choose the same dot again to clear it. Set a color on several items. Select them and edit them together. The sheet has a Co
Write a note on any item in Get Info. Quick Open shows the note under the item's name. Spotlight includes it in the description. Notes are plain text and stay in your library.

Save text you type often, such as an address or a standard reply, as a snippet. To add one, choose File > New Snippet…, or click Snippets in the Library window. To copy a snippet, type its name or a keyword in Quick Open, then press Return.

Library works with other apps in four ways: the library:// address, which other apps and web pages can open; Add to Library in the Services menu; Spotlight, which finds your items in any search; the Shortcuts app, which has actions for opening and searching items, adding bookmarks and apps, the clipboard, and terminal commands.

Library handles links that start with library://. A link never opens the Edit Library window. It does one of the following three things. Link What it does library://open?name=NAME Opens the bookmark or application named NAME library://open?name=NAME&value=VALUE Opens the bookmark or application named NAME, and fills its template with VALUE library://menu Shows the Library menu library://search Ope

How the name is matched The name must match an item's name exactly, ignoring case. Library does not match part of a name. Library looks at bookmarks, applications, and dividers, in the order they appear in the library. It uses the first item that matches. Folders are never matched. Terminal commands are never matched, so a link can never run one. Items in Recently Deleted are not matched. A divide

How the value is used If the bookmark has exactly one field in its address, value fills it, and Library does not ask for a value. If the bookmark has more than one field, Library asks for all of them in one sheet, and value is ignored. If the bookmark is a template and no value is given, Library asks for the value. Spaces in a value must be encoded as %20. A value is used as typed. Library asks yo

t: What the scheme does not do
s: What the scheme does not do It does not open commands, so a web page cannot run a terminal command with it. It does not show a window, and it does not change your library. Unknown hosts, such as library://something, and any other parameters are ignored. Anything that can open a library:// link can open a bookmark or an application in your library by its name. A plain bookmark or application opens

Library adds two items to the Services menu, both named Add to Library: one adds a selected web link, and one adds applications and folders selected in the Finder. They appear in the Services menu of most apps, and in the Finder's right-click Services menu.

t: Add a link from any app
s: Add a link from any app Select a web address in an app, such as a page address in a document or a message. Choose Services > Add to Library. The selection must be one web address that starts with http:// or https://. A bare domain, such as example.com, is not accepted here, though Quick Open accepts it. The selection can be up to 4,096 characters. Spaces and line breaks around it are ignored. The

t: Add applications and folders from the Finder
s: Add applications and folders from the Finder Select one or more applications or folders in the Finder. Choose Services > Add to Library. Each application is added by its name and path. Each folder is added as a link to the folder. Choosing a folder opens it in the Finder. Applications and folders already in the library are skipped. Other files in the selection are ignored. If nothing in the select

t: If the Services items do not appear
s: If the Services items do not appear Log out and back in, or run /System/Library/CoreServices/pbs -update in Terminal. Library asks macOS to refresh its services each time it starts.

Library adds its items to the Spotlight index, so Spotlight can find them. What is indexed Every bookmark, application, terminal command, and template that opens something. Not folders, dividers, or items in Recently Deleted. What Spotlight sees for each item Title: the item's name. Description: the address, command, or application path, with the item's note on the line below it. Keywords: the ite

Library provides these actions to the Shortcuts app: Action What it does Open Library Item Opens a bookmark or an application. Its optional Value fills the {} placeholder in a template's address. Library asks for the value when it is left empty. Search Library Returns the bookmarks and applications that match the text. Folders, dividers, and terminal commands are left out. Add Bookmark to Library

The URL scheme handles only the three hosts above. Any other library:// link is ignored. Services accepts one web address of up to 4,096 characters, or applications and folders. Spotlight indexes all openable items, and updates about 0.8 seconds after a change. Shortcuts results are limited as listed in Shortcuts app: five items for Frequently Used, 20 for Search Clipboard History. Only Run Termin

While Library runs, it checks GitHub for a new release every hour. It also checks at launch if the last check was an hour or more ago. Quit Library. Move Library.app from your Applications folder to the Trash. Older versions kept a copy of the source in ~/Library/Application Support/Library. If that folder exists, move it to the Trash too. Your library and clipboard history stay in ~/.library. Removing the app doesn't remove that folder. Run./build.sh to build the app. On GitHub Actions, a pull request that changes code runs./test.sh. A push to main also builds the app and renders the screens. Changes to Markdown and docs/ skip the run.
Run./test.sh to run the checks in Tests/. The checks use private pasteboards and temporary files. They never touch your clipboard or your library.
